title: Silicon Valley is falling in line with Trump's attempt to rename AI
key_facts: The Verge argues that some of Silicon Valley's most powerful figures are following President Trump's attempt to rebrand artificial intelligence as 'super intelligence', while most of the broader population is sticking with 'AI'.
Elon Musk promised to rename SpaceXAI to SpaceXSI.

Hours after Trump declared that the White House considers anyone who uses 'Artificial Intelligence' instead of 'Super Intelligence' 'THE ENEMY', Marc Benioff announced that Salesforce would rename AIForce to SIForce.

Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang attended the summit where the executive order requiring agencies to use 'super intelligence' was announced; Nvidia said it would 'commit' $1 billion to scientific advancement, including 'super intelligence research'.

Microsoft's Satya Nadella, who attended the same AI summit as Huang, Zuckerberg, Pichai, Bezos, Amodei and Musk, repeatedly called the technology 'super intelligence' in a post 'yesterday' calling for an 'emergency brake' for AI.
The Verge says that during Trump's second term Silicon Valley has repeatedly tried to ingratiate itself with the administration, after a more contentious first term.
The article is commentary; its words 'capitulated' and 'caved' are the outlet's opinion.
quote_evidence: When President Donald Trump announced his plans to rebrand artificial intelligence as "super intelligence," you'd be forgiven for being skeptical that it would catch on.
The latest to cave is Microsoft's Satya Nadella, who attended the same AI summit as Huang along with Mark Zuckerberg, Sundar Pichai, Jeff Bezos, Dario Amodei, and Musk.
During Trump's second term, Silicon Valley has repeatedly tried to ingratiate itself with the administration, after having a much more contentious relationship during his first term.
why_it_matters_hint: A tech outlet counts the executives who have adopted the White House's 'super intelligence' wording, adding Microsoft's chief to a list we have followed since 4 Oct.
event_date: Commentary of 11 Oct 2026 on events of 4 to 10 Oct 2026 (Nadella's post on 10 Oct)
notes: Commentary, not news reporting; the executives' reasons are the outlet's reading. Earlier stories carried: Trump's 8 Oct post (The Independent, 9 Oct 2026 edition); Benioff's SIForce (Business Insider, 10 Oct edition); Nadella's 10 Oct post (TechCrunch, 11 Oct edition); Musk's SpaceXSI plan (5 Oct edition).
